To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
in patients with advanced hepatocellular cancer, first-line therapy combining sorafenib with resminostat showed no significant efficacy over sorafenib alone.
the combination of resminostat and sorafenib was safe but did not improve the efficacy of sorafenib alone in patients with advanced hepatocellular cancer (HCC).
resminostat at a dose of 400 mg plus sorafenib did not improve efficacy over sorafenib alone as a first-line therapy for patients with advanced HCCA.

the development of a new method of treating hepatocellular carcinoma.
the study of phase I/II of the first line of the treatment of advanced hepatocellular cancer with sorafenib in combination with resminostat in east Asian patients.
the development of an efficient, low cost and environmentally friendly method for the preparation of 2-phenylquinoline derivatives.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combination therapy with sorafeinib plus resminostat is not superior to sorafenib alone in terms of efficacy, and that the safety profile of the combination therapy was not improved.
resminostat in combination with sorafenib is not a viable therapeutic option for advanced HCC.
the combination of resminostat with sorafenib was not superior to sorafenib alone in terms of TTP/OS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination therapy with sorafeinib plus resminostat did not show a significant efficacy advantage over the sorafeinib monotherapy.
resminostat at 400 mg plus sorafenib is safe and tolerable, with a similar safety profile to sorafenib alone.
resminostat at a recommended dose of 400 mg per day plus sorafenib is well tolerated and has no significant efficacy advantage in patients with advanced hepatocellular cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
resminostat plus low dose sorafenib (600 mg/day) should be evaluated as a first-line therapy for HCC in future clinical trials.
combination therapy with resminostat plus sorafenib is feasible, safe, and tolerable in advanced HCC patients.
the combination of resminostat and sorafenib did not show any significant benefit in terms of overall survival and time to progression in patients with advanced hepatocellular cancer.
